myths.title: The story of Eurṓpē
myths.text: Eurṓpē appears in greek location tradition as a figure whose domain over personified continent of europe shapes both cosmic order and human experience. The surviving narratives emphasize Eurṓpē's role, attributes, and relationships with other powers.

lore.syncretism: Greek cult and myth travelled with colonists, traders, and conquerors; Roman adaptation, Hellenistic ruler cult, and later European classicism all recast this name for new audiences.
lore.culturalLegacy: The name endures in place names, scholarly vocabulary, modern fiction, and the ongoing recovery of ancient Greek culture through archaeology and philology. Restoring Eurṓpē in Unicode preserves the name's cultural specificity against the flattening force of plain ASCII.
lore.extendedMeditation: Names are not merely labels; they are compressed worlds. Eurṓpē carries within it a greek location understanding of broad-faced (from εὐρύς + ὤψ). Unicode restoration returns that world to readable form.
sources: Homer. Iliad and Odyssey; Hesiod. Theogony and Works and Days.
Beekes, R. S. P. Etymological Dictionary of Greek. Leiden: Brill, 2010.
Material evidence from the Greek world — inscriptions, sanctuaries, votive deposits, and literary papyri — anchors the name in historical cult.
